title: 3.2.6 Contract Administration.pdf
visual_method: PyMuPDF rendered 1.2x; six-slide contact sheets opened with view_image; extracted page text crosschecked against all slides. Page ranges refer to physical PDF pages, not printed slide numbers.

objective_topic_mapping.objective_or_topic: TLO 3: PMO, PCO, ACO, COR, PI, SUPSHIP and RMC
TLO 4: unilateral change order/bilateral supplemental agreement
TLO 5: NECP/ECP, approval levels, VE, deviation/waiver, modification requests and process diagrams
TLO 8: ADR, disputes and appeal diagram

findings.original_claim: Reclamas are a Level 1 approval trigger
findings.required_change: Move reclama filed by an SPM CCB member or change sponsor to Level 2. Label hierarchy a coursebook shipbuilding model subject to current delegations.
findings.explanation: Guide misplaced a Level 2 bullet under Level 1.

findings.original_claim: DCMA and DCAA perform transaction processing
findings.required_change: Remove transaction-processing entries for DCMA/DCAA; retain DFAS payment/transaction role. Add DCMA support extends preaward through completion.
findings.source_basis: Coursebook pp7,10; existing agency official sources
findings.explanation: Slide has blank financial-column cells for DCMA/DCAA.

findings.original_claim: NECP/ECP and FMR/HMR distinctions compressed and workflow diagrams omitted
findings.required_change: Distinguish nonconfiguration NECP from configuration ECP; field-origin FMR and PM-origin HMR approvals support warranted KO action. Explain SUPSHIP higher-level vs local routes and RMC conditions-found, scope, funding, estimate, negotiation, signed modification sequence.
findings.explanation: Program approval/funding is not authority to modify contract.

findings.required_change: After receipt of KO decision: agency board appeal within 90 days OR action in COFC within 12 months, subject to CDA provisions; do not depict alternatives as sequential mandatory appeals.
findings.explanation: Image-only decision tree omitted from guide.

findings.original_claim: Cure notices always provide 10 days; delays automatically excused
findings.guide_location: Termination Types and Notices; Government Obligation to Pay
findings.required_change: Cure period 10 days or longer if necessary for applicable progress/other failures; delivery default may not require advance cure. Excusable delay requires beyond-control, no-fault/no-negligence showing under applicable clause, not merely a listed event. Termination notice does not automatically give a new cure period.
findings.explanation: List of examples is not automatic entitlement; preserve corrected constructive-change treatment.

findings.required_change: Allowable incurred costs, necessary termination work, settlements and adjusted fee depend on applicable clause/settlement; no automatic payment for anticipated profit on unperformed work.
findings.explanation: Distinguish cost reimbursement from blanket recovery.

findings.required_change: COTS is a qualifying commercial product sold in substantial marketplace quantities, offered without modification in same form, excluding bulk cargo; not a generic term for all commercial services.
findings.explanation: Boundary matters for commercial product classification.

notes: All 46 physical PDF pages reviewed including lifecycle chart p7, organization table p10, approval table pp23-24, SUPSHIP flow p26, disputes diagram p32 and dense RMC flow p46.
Shipbuilding hierarchy and process examples are explicitly attributed to coursebook; no claim that current local delegations were independently re-certified.
blockers: Current signed local shipbuilding/RMC delegation packages not supplied; preserve illustrative coursebook status.
implementation_status: Recommendations only; guide edits owned by integrating agent.
